[PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
## Consolidated Experience from Similar Tasks
Consolidated lessons from navigation and manipulation: (1) Movement predictions can fail if obstacles block the path. Before moving toward a target, check the route for obstacles and choose a clear path or adjust movement instead of assuming forward motion will succeed. (2) A movement obstruction does not imply the target is out of reach for interaction; check actual proximity before predicting pickup failure. (3) Pick attempts require an empty hand; verify the hand is empty or place/drop any held object first. (4) Find actions may fail because the target is not present/visible or the skill cannot identify it; do not assume the target is available, explore alternate locations and confirm object availability. General principle: verify action preconditions—clear path, empty hand, target proximity, and object presence—before acting, and avoid over-inferring from one failure mode to another.

## Preliminary Thinking
For the current cooking/pickup task: 1) Locate the potato and identify relevant obstacles (e.g., stool) in the environment. 2) Before moving, inspect the intended path; if blocked, plan a route around the obstacle rather than moving directly forward. 3) Ensure the robot's hand is empty; if not, place/drop the held object first. 4) Move to a position where the potato is within pick range, but do not assume a movement obstruction means it is unreachable—check actual proximity. 5) Attempt Pick once preconditions are met; if it fails, diagnose whether the cause is range, hand state, or object availability. 6) For put-away tasks, if a find action fails, do not assume the object is absent; explore the environment, check alternate locations, and confirm availability before retrying.
[/PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
